source.title: Selecting the best optimizers for deep learning–based medical image segmentation
source.authors: Aliasghar Mortazi; V. Çiçek; Elif Keleş; Ulas Bagci

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer effects on held-out segmentation performance in a new setting: cardiac MRI segmentation.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports test-set Dice scores by architecture, optimizer, and structure, including averages. The training and validation curves and cited optimizer results are not additional test-set rows. No explicit training error is reported.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam with Nesterov and cyclic learning-rate training using held-out cardiac MRI segmentation Dice. This tests V4's optimizer-ranking question in a new setting, although the tuning protocol is insufficiently reported to establish its limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute better segmentation generalization to CLMR's cyclic learning and momentum schedules and also claim computational efficiency. Their evidence compares CLMR with Adam, not multiple adaptive optimizers, and does not establish a training-to-test gap or statistically significant superiority.
record.recipe_differences: Applies a proposed cyclic learning/momentum optimizer to cardiac MRI segmentation and compares it with Adam, Nesterov, and CLR; this is a new task setting and method.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer ranking varies by architecture: Adam beats CLR on U-Net average test Dice, while CLR exceeds Adam on the other three architectures; CLMR exceeds Adam on all four.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed CLMR achieves higher average test Dice than Adam for all four architectures after a dedicated cyclic-parameter search.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jointly cycling learning rate and momentum can improve cardiac MRI segmentation performance relative to the tested Adam configuration.

record.problems: Only one cardiac MRI dataset/task is tested; the paper gives no uncertainty estimates and no training-set performance for a direct training-to-test gap comparison. Conclusions about generalization are therefore based on held-out test Dice and may not extend to other medical imaging settings.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports test Dice separately for RV, Myo., and LV in Table 2. Those structure-specific rows are omitted to stay within the 60-row cap; the average rows are retained for each architecture and optimizer.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.

The specified classification and language benchmarks; a documented comparable learning-rate and decay-only tuning budget; equal or better training performance; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and word-level language modeling.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 average values and Table 1 parameter counts match the record. Structure-specific results are already declared in rows_left_out. The paper does not report Adam or fixed-Nesterov tuning details, repeated-run uncertainty, or training-set performance. Its architecture comparisons do not test V2 or V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

Tests adaptive Adam against Nesterov, CLR, and CLMR on cardiac MRI segmentation; does not report training performance or test an SGD/momentum-SGD comparison on the listed image-classification or language benchmarks.

relationships.condition: Adam versus fixed Nesterov, all four architectures on ACDC segmentation after 100 epochs
relationships.reason: Adam has higher average test Dice in every architecture (R1–R2, R5–R6, R9–R10, R13–R14), identifying a setting where the adaptive-worse tendency does not hold; comparable tuning is undocumented.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved higher average test Dice across all architectures, but these comparisons remain unverified and comparable tuning was undocumented.

relationships.condition: Adam versus CLR, U-Net on ACDC segmentation
relationships.reason: Adam scores 0.8813 versus CLR's 0.8714 (R5, R7), showing that a cyclic learning-rate comparator does not consistently outperform Adam.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly exceeded the cyclic-learning-rate comparator's Dice score, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Adam versus CLR, Enc Dec and both DenseNets on ACDC segmentation
relationships.reason: CLR exceeds Adam by 0.0267, 0.0061, and 0.0140 average Dice respectively (R1, R3, R9, R11, R13, R15); these modest advantages support the direction, with tuning comparability and uncertainty unresolved.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher average Dice scores for CLR than Adam remain unverified, with tuning comparability and uncertainty unresolved.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
